What works with what

Source: vignettes/articles/capabilities.Rmd
capabilities.Rmd

Each kernel was fitted to a small simulated data set (24 species, one in the tree but not fitted) and every feature was tried; ✓ means it ran, – means it is not defined for that kernel (see the notes). Kernels without a k_white() term behave like the same kernel with one. The table is made by data-raw/capabilities.R in the package sources, so it can be rerun after any change.

k_bm() + k_slope(x) * k_white() ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ – d – d ✓

Columns starting with … refer to several rows per species.

a Latent values (rates, slopes, t multipliers) are sampled, so these kernels need method = "sample".
b Ancestral states need a process along the tree; dense components (k_dist(), k_slope(latent = FALSE)) have none.
c Ancestral states are not defined for varying slopes (the slope at a node has no trait value).
d With several rows per species, use one latent k_slope(x) * k term with a branch-wise k.
